newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FALKIRK IN SEMIFINALS FOR FIRST TIME FOR 40 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FALKIRK IN SEMIFINALS FOR FIRST TIME FOR 40 YEARS.

text.p: First division Falkirk reached the semifinals of the Scottish F.A. Cup for the first time for 40 years on Saturday with a 2-0 victory over premier division rivals Raith.
Greenock Morton failed to match that achievement and went down 5-2 at home to Kilmarnock while Dundee United beat Motherwell 4-1 in the all-premier division quarter-final.
Favourites Celtic are already into the last four after beating Rangers 2-0 on Thursday.
The day's only premier division match saw Hibernian collect vital points in their battle against relegation courtesy of a 1-0 home win over Dunfermline.
Falkirk last reached the semifinals in 1957 when they went on to win the Cup for the second time in their 121-year history.
Kevin James gave them the lead on Saturday in the 44th minute and the victory was completed 10 minutes from time with a David Hagen header.
Raith had two efforts cleared off the goal-line.
Dundee United, Cup winners in 1994, found their form to overwhelm Motherwell with a second half onslaught.
Andy McLaren got things going just after the break and Robbie Winters made it 2-0 in the 66th minute. McLaren and Kjell Olofsson completed the scoring spree.
Kilmarnock were three up at halftime and cruising against 10-man Morton but were given a scare after the break.
Two goals by John Henry and one from Paul Wright, together with the sending-off of Seve McCahill, looked to have settled the issue in their favour.

But two goals in 10 minutes by Morton's Alan Mahood forced Kilmarnock to up the pace. Jim McIntyre restored their two-goal lead and then Henry put the icing on the cake when he completed his hat-trick.
Keith Wright struck with a volley after 11 minutes to give Hibs their first league win since December and put the brakes on a slide that threatened to go all the way to the first division.
